cards.front: Recall a key point about The Role of the Church
cards.back: Jesus taught "Love your neighbour as yourself" (Mark 12:31) and the Parable of the Good Samaritan (Luke 10:25-37) shows that Christians must help anyone in need, regardless of who they are. The local church puts this teaching into practice.

cards.back: 1. For The Role of the Church questions, always include specific scriptural or source references where relevant 2. Explain both religious and non-religious viewpoints 3. Link your discussion of The Role of the Church to its real-world impact on believers and society

Students often think all Christians celebrate the Eucharist in the same way. Wrong: "All Christians believe the bread and wine literally become Jesus' body and blood." Correct: "Catholics believe in transubstantiation; Protestants have different views including consubstantiation and memorial symbolism."

cards.front: Assessment Objective Focus: The Role of the Church
cards.back: AO1 — Knowledge: Show precise knowledge of The Role of the Church, using specialist vocabulary and referring to sources of wisdom and authority (e.g. scripture, sacred texts).

cards.front: Understanding The Role of the Church in Christian Practice
cards.back: The Role of the Church is a key aspect of Christian practice that GCSE Religious Studies students must understand in depth. Christianity is the world’s largest religion with over 2 billion followers, and its practices shape the daily lives of believers. cards.front: Biblical and Theological Foundations of The Role of the Church
cards.back: Christian practices are grounded in the Bible and developed through church tradition. cards.front: The Impact of The Role of the Church on Christians Today
cards.back: Understanding the role of the church in the modern world means considering how Christians practice their faith in contemporary Britain and globally. Christianity in the UK is diverse: the Church of England (Anglican) is the established church, but there are also Catholic, Methodist, Baptist, Pentecostal and Orthodox communities, each with distinct approaches to the role of the church.
